en: Amoghapāśakalparāja (VI) 82a 5. ||
Therefore, I shall now proclaim the ritual procedure for the fire offering (*homa*) of the maṇḍala of liberation;
by it, one is completely liberated from all sins and obscurations,
as well as from all sufferings, defilements, and the terrible oceans of afflictions (*kleśa*).
The crossing over by means of the essence is accomplished;
it is the irreversible state, the unsurpassed.
It brings comfort to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; it is the supreme vision of the supramundane path of all Buddhas, and indeed the very vision of the Bodhisattvas.
The transition to the gods is immediate, as soon as the oblation is offered; of this there is no doubt. [This applies to] Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara.
Īśvara, Maheśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and even Kārttikeya—
all these come at once by this mere oblation; of this there is no doubt.

Gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and asuras; together with garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, and kumbhāṇḍas—all arrive at that very moment. They all prostrate at the feet of the vidyādhara by the hundreds, and they protect him on all sides day and night.
The four great kings, whose great selves possess the vajra in their hands,
and the ten great lords of yakṣas protect the ten directions;
they ward off wicked and evil people.
Immediately thereafter, they ward off all those terrifying and fearful hells, as well as all sinful and wicked beings;
then the great Meru of merit proceeds, an unsurpassed mass of great merit.
Twenty palas of sandalwood, five palas of agarwood, and always seven palas of turuṣka; one part each of camphor and musk, and the fruit [quantity] of saffron should be used;
five palas of kundruka and always seven palas of guggulu.
Having ground them together in one place, one should mix white sugar with honey and form pills the size of an *akṣa*.

Having kindled the fire with fuel-sticks of fragrant wood, *arka* wood, and *samī* wood, one should offer one thousand and eight mustard seeds mixed with parched grain (*lāja*) along with the pills smeared with ghee.
Whenever one performs the rite of oblation, one should offer exactly one thousand and eight [of these].
At those times, they exhaust all evil, obscurations, and defilements;
at those times, they are completely liberated from all diseases;
at those times, they are completely liberated from all ailments.
At those times, in Jambūdvīpa, they cause all the obstructions of evil for all beings—men, women, boys, girls, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and so forth—to be exhausted.

They pacify all fears of armies, all epidemics, all calamities, all misfortunes, all planetary influences, all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes, all fears of one's own army or the enemy's army, all fears of adversaries and enemies, and all fears of thieves,
rogues, robbers, and fierce wild beasts.
And all those beings who smell that fragrance shall become fearless.

Whether they be women, men, boys, or girls; whether śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, or śūdras—all of them shall become irreversible and shall be set forth toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Upon their birth, they will all travel to the world-system of Sukhāvatī;
they will be born from spontaneously produced lotuses.
And all those belonging to the animal realm—whether two-legged or four-legged—will, by the mere scent of that fragrance, certainly become non-retrogressive [in their progress toward enlightenment].
They shall attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in the state of non-retrogression.
O holder of all vidyās, in whatever manner one performs the homa, in that same manner his body shall become perfectly stainless and purified.
When one thousand and eight [recitations] are complete, the body of the vidyādhara blazes;
he beholds the great forms of the Buddhas in the ten directions,
and those forms of the Tathāgatas utter words of praise for the vidyādhara.
Excellent, excellent, Vidyādhara! This is the supreme mandala of the secret liberation of all Tathāgatas, the supramundane ritual procedure for the fire offering (homa).
This is the great ritual procedure for the fire offering that crushes all Māras.
This is the unsurpassed path to enlightenment.
Then all those forms of the Tathāgatas extend their right arms, which are the color of gold, and place their hands upon the head of the vidyādhara.
Then Āryāvalokiteśvara appears before him in his own form.
Adorned with all ornaments,
wearing the attire of Brahmā as Amoghapāśa, decorated with a crown of matted locks, and holding a lotus, a trident, and a noose—
he speaks to the vidyādhara.

Excellent, excellent, O Vidyādhara Siddha! By you has been [revealed] the Amoghapāśahṛdaya, the Vimokṣamaṇḍala, and the procedure for the world-surpassing great fire-offering. Grant the boon as you pray; I give it all to you.
Then the Vidyādhara should utter his desired boons;
he shall obtain all of them.
Noble Avalokiteśvara extends his arms and places his hand upon the head of the Vidyādhara.
As soon as it is placed upon the hand, the vidyādhara travels through the sky;
he traverses all the buddha-fields in the ten directions and obtains the direct vision of all the Tathāgatas.
A. 83a 1. They attain the state of non-retrogression;
they receive the prophecy from all Tathāgatas in all Buddha-fields.
(They receive the prophecy from all Tathāgatas in all Buddha-fields.)
Having attended upon all the buddha-fields, they proceed to the world-system of Sukhāvatī; there,
in the presence of the Tathāgata Amitābha and his assembly of excellent bodhisattvas, they shall hear the teaching of the Dharma.
"Until the very end at the seat of awakening.
Therefore, I shall describe the supreme, supramundane site for the fire sacrifice (*homasthāna*):
having fashioned a blooming lotus measuring three cubits in circumference.
Provided with earth and cow dung,
one should dig a pit in the center of the filaments of the lotus, measuring one cubit in depth.
Then, having drawn a triangle all around, one should place sixteen or five petals in the center.
One should adorn the lotus with various multicolored hues;
outside the perimeter of the lotus, one should fashion a square mandala,
and adorn it with various excellent fragrances.
Around the perimeter of the mandala, there are four full vases filled with silver vessels; four water-offering bowls (arghapādyāni) filled with silver vessels;
and four [vessels] for various perfumes.
Filling golden vessels with various kinds of delicious foods and placing them of three white varieties.
Likewise, having arranged various fruits and diverse kinds, one should scatter various flowers.
Arranging them with various types of garlands all around the maṇḍala, one should adorn it with five-colored banners.
And having placed well-adorned vases, divided at the four gates—
It is filled with scented water. At the four gates, the *Prajñāpāramitā* should be recited, together with the assembly of well-adorned Dharma-preachers.
In the four corners, one should recite the *Amoghapāśasūtra*.
One should worship the Dharma-seat of the well-adorned Dharma-preacher with golden flowers, silver flowers, copper flowers,
and the seven precious gems.
Then, the Vidyādhara— pure, wearing clean garments, well-bathed, and perfumed with fragrant scents—
should recite the Amoghapāśahṛdaya over the pill one hundred and eight times.
Having consecrated it one hundred and eight times with the Krodharāja mantra, [he should proceed].
One should recite the Amoghavilokita-hṛdaya one hundred and eight times.
Thereafter, one should offer oblations one thousand and eight times into the Amoghajvalana-vimokṣa-maṇḍala with the Pāśa-hṛdaya mantra.
By not engaging in conversation, one should possess a mind of loving-kindness and a heart of compassion and pity; this is the unsurpassed action.
Homage to the Triple Gem!
Homage to the noble Āryāvalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Greatly Compassionate One!
It is thus: Oṃ padmapāṇi dhara dhara padmabhuje!
Blaze, blaze, O fire! Bhuru, bhuru, O you whose arms grant liberation! Burn, burn all impurities, O Amoghapāṇi, bestower of boons! Hūṃ hūṃ!
Completely consume my sins!
O Peaceful One, who brings peace, the savior of the world;
O Bestower of Wishes through Your Universal Radiance!
Turu turu, O most excellent Amoghasiddhi!
Oṃ bhūr bhuva, homage be to you, svāhā!
This is the supramundane and unsurpassed ritual for the fire-offering (*homa*) of the *dhāraṇī* of the Great Noose, the Heart of the Mandala for the Emission of Flames.
Then, that *vidyādhara* should perform all his wondrous tasks with those ashes;
and whatever [beings] fall upon his body with those ashes, [they shall be liberated].

He becomes completely liberated from all obscurations and sins. By making a *tilaka* on the forehead, one is immediately freed from quartan fever— whether it be every second day, every third day, or that which occurs nightly or daily.
The midnight [meal],
the midday [meal],
and the [meal] at dawn.

Annual fevers, monthly fevers, seven-day fevers, continuous fevers, and chills—none of these shall remain. Having applied a *tilaka* on the crown of the head, one is liberated from eight million four hundred thousand planetary spirits (*graha*).
And all [spirits] flee for thousands of *yojanas* in the ten directions, even at a distance of a hundred *yojanas*.
And all [the obstructors] flee for ten thousand yojanas in the ten directions.

One should scatter ashes or dust toward the wind; wherever they fall from that place and in whatever direction, there the yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, pretas, kumbhāṇḍas, apasmāras, vighnas, and vināyakas shall no longer remain.
All stand still and flee;
it is no longer possible to advance to that place.
By applying a *tilaka* on the location of the heart, one is liberated from all diseases.
By applying a *tilaka* at the navel, one is immediately liberated from all diseases located within the abdomen.
By touching one bitten by poison, that person shall become free of poison. One should give it to one intoxicated by poison, and they shall become free of poison.

One should bathe with ashes; all *kākhorda* spells, poisons, and mantras will be destroyed. For various types of leprosy, scrofula, ringworm, pustules, copper-colored warts, poison-eruptions, and all forms of *dadru*, one should stir [the ashes] with warm water and apply them.
One should smear [the area] with ghee over which the mantra has been recited seven times; immediately one is liberated from all diseases.
If one throws [ashes] toward a cloud, all cold winds and hailstones will not fall.
One should cast [the breath] toward the wind; the binding of the wind is thus accomplished.
One should cast it in the four directions;
this becomes the binding of the great boundary.
Immediately thereafter, one should sprinkle [the area] in a circular pattern with all kinds of flowers, fruits, crops, flowering trees,
shrubs, groves, gardens, parks, and mountains.
All grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, and forest trees shall become self-protected.

A great boundary-binding will be established in a circular perimeter extending for a hundred yojanas in every direction. (A great boundary-binding will be established in a circular perimeter extending for a hundred yojanas in every direction.)

He shall dwell at the four city gates. Whatever beings enter or exit there— women, men, boys, girls, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, those born as animals, bipeds, quadrupeds, beasts, and birds— all of them shall become free from the obscurations of evil.
By merely leaping over it, one is completely liberated from the suffering of all diseases;
one becomes free from all ailments and,
upon the transition of birth, proceeds to the world-system of Sukhāvatī.
They attain the state of non-retrogression and shall remain so until they abide in Buddhahood.
Or, one may scatter ashes over a corpse in a cemetery or upon a funeral pyre.
And those beings who have been reborn in hell will all immediately fall away from hell;
they will be reborn either in Abhirati or in Sukhāvatī.

Whether one sprinkles it around a city, a monastery, a temple, a village, a house, or a forest hermitage in every direction, there will be a great binding of the boundary and a great pacification. If one sprinkles it at the gate of a royal palace, the king, together with his harem and retinue, becomes well-protected.
One should sprinkle [the name] of the Great Being amidst all enemies.
By the mere act of sprinkling, all those people will become free from the obscurations of evil;
they will also become free from disease and sin.
One performs hundreds of thousands of other tasks;
one should apply one's own opinion and one's own intelligence everywhere. Thus it is said.
Therefore, in this maṇḍala of liberation, I shall proclaim the Heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa, the supramundane cloth.
On a cloth or on fine Chinese silk, well-cleaned and properly stretched,
measuring two cubits, three cubits, or four cubits in size.
There, in the center, one should draw Lokeśvara Amoghapāśa, wearing the attire of Brahmā and adorned with a crown of matted locks.
He wears a crown bearing the Victorious One Amitābha and holds a crescent moon in his right hand.
He has four arms, is adorned with all ornaments, and sits in the paryanka posture.
Mount Potalaka should be depicted strewn with various flowering creepers and strewn with various jewel-creepers; upon it, a lion throne should be fashioned.
2. Adorned with all ornaments, a lotus seat should be fashioned upon the lion throne.
Upon that, the noble Avalokiteśvara should be depicted seated, holding a lotus and a trident, bearing a noose, and possessing his full form.
His hand should be in the gesture of granting reassurance, and above his head there should be a gabled celestial palace (*kūṭāgāra-vimāna*) inlaid with various divine jewels.
It has the form of a railing.
Upon the railing, seven Tathāgatas are to be fashioned,
adorned with all ornaments, seated upon lotus thrones according to the proper proportions.

Above that Tathāgata, in the center of the gabled pavilion (kūṭāgāra), three Tathāgatas are to be fashioned, adorned with all ornaments and seated in the cross-legged posture: Vairocana, Amitābha, and the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvaraprabha.
Furthermore, Āryāvalokiteśvara is to be fashioned surrounded by a circle extending for thirty-two yojanas, arrayed with thirty-two Tathāgatas.
With the circular mandala of the Tathāgata, various blazing rays of light should be produced;
and a garland of tridents should also be made for him alone. (6)
Thirty-two deities are to be fashioned for the circular [mandala].
In the center above, Vajradhara is to be fashioned with a distorted face and a wrathful expression, brandishing a vajra.
Then Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara,
the sons of the gods Īśvara and Maheśvara, Indra, the sons of the gods of the Trayastriṃśa heaven, the Akaniṣṭha gods, the Tuṣita gods,
and the Nirmita gods.

The sons of the gods Candra and Sūrya, the four Great Kings— Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Kumāra— the deities Agni, Mahākāla, Nandikeśvara, Nanda, Upananda, Baladeva, Pūrṇabhadra, and Māṇibhadra, the Śuddhāvāsa deities, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin deities.
The sons of the gods (devaputra) are to be fashioned; a circle of deities (devatāparimaṇḍala) is to be made, and garlands of lotuses (samantapadmamālā) are to be fashioned all around.
A lotus garland surrounded on all sides by tridents (triśūla) with vajras, extending from the hand, is to be made.
They are to be depicted holding various flowers, various jewels (maṇiratna), and various weapons, and a garland of flames (jvālāmālā) is to be fashioned all around.
On the right side, Noble Tārā should be depicted seated in the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka),
gazing up at the face of Noble Avalokiteśvara,
holding a blue lotus, a jewel, and a gem in her hands, and adorned with all ornaments.
Behind him, Bhṛkuṭī should be depicted, holding various flowers and adorned with all ornaments.
To the left, Śvetā should be depicted, seated in the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka),
holding a night-lotus (kumuda) and a jewel in her hands, gazing at Avalokiteśvara, and adorned with various ornaments.

Behind her, Padmasundarī should be depicted as white, holding various flowers and adorned with all ornaments. Below the white Tārā-devī, the ten Pāramitās should be depicted; they are all standing with heads bowed, wearing white garments, and adorned with all ornaments.

On the right side, the Rākṣasī Ekajaṭā should be depicted as fierce, seated in the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka), with four arms holding a noose, an axe, a sword, and a vajra; she gazes at Āryāvalokiteśvara. To her left, a female messenger (dūtī) should be depicted with a mouth made terrifying by fangs, adorned with all ornaments, and possessing four arms holding a vajra, an axe, and a noose.
Seated with a trident in hand and in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*),
she should be depicted gazing at Lokeśvara, who is ablaze within his inner core, on Mount Potalaka.
In the space between them, the Naga kings Nanda and Upananda should be depicted together with their palaces and Naga maidens;
they should be shown holding various flowers and lifting the Blessed One, Lokeśvara, above them.

At the foot of the mountain, Anopamya, Vāsantī, Pṛthivī, Devatā, Śrī, Abhimā, Sarasvatī, Śaṅkhalā, and Saṃkhinī should be depicted, all adorned with their own ornaments and holding various flowers, jewels, and gems.

They should be made. Upon the summit of the gabled pavilion (kūṭāgāra), a single row of the eight great terrifying caityas should be made; it should be adorned just as the ornamentation of a caitya is decorated.

Below the caitya, on the right side, the approach to the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) should be made, and the Blessed One Lokeśvara should be depicted there, facing [the caitya] and performing worship.
The Noble Vajradhara should be depicted with a fly-whisk in his hand. Below him, ṛṣis and sons of gods should be depicted,
worshipping the Blessed One with various flowers.

The turning of the Wheel of Dharma is to be depicted on the left side. Ānanda, the Vajradhara, with a fly-whisk in his hand, is to be depicted fanning [the Buddha]. To the right of the Blessed One, facing him, Āryāvalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa is to be depicted worshipping the Blessed One. On the left side, Krodharāja is to be depicted worshipping the Blessed One. Beneath him, a host of ṛṣis and deities is to be depicted worshipping the Blessed One.

On the left and right sides of Duṣya, on the exterior all around, one hundred and eight images of Tathāgatas should be made; they should be depicted according to their proper proportions, seated in the paryanka posture upon lotus seats. They should be adorned with ornaments. A Vidyādhara should be depicted at the base of the lion throne of the noble Avalokiteśvara, prostrating himself with his knees on the ground, holding in his hands a flower and a censer.
The face of Noble Avalokiteśvara should be fashioned.

One must be pure, well-bathed, and wear clean garments; one must have eaten various delicious foods and white meals. [The image] should be painted on a clean, new vessel using non-sticky pigments. Furthermore, one must avoid various kinds of bad food and poor clothing, and abstain from intoxicants, meat, onions, garlic, leeks, and impure mixtures. (8)
6. One must be resolute; one must bathe daily with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*);
one must be free from impurity, stinginess, and envy;
and one must be devoted to loving-kindness, compassion, and the highest resolve, intent upon faith in the Three Jewels.
It should be painted on a cloth made of fine silk;
it should be painted with various pigments perfumed with camphor and musk.
One must remain undisturbed and avoid the company of crowds.
One must be free from sloth and torpor;
one should indeed be thus well-prepared through the performance of one's duties.
It should be performed;
it should be painted during the bright fortnight,
and not during the dark fortnight.
It should be painted under a highly auspicious lunar mansion and on a very propitious day.
It should be commenced on an auspicious lunar day,
under the Puṣya constellation,
which is praised by all Tathāgatas and empowered by all Bodhisattvas.
"It is blessed by all the deities.
Any son of good family or daughter of good family, or monk or nun, or layman or laywoman;
or a śramaṇa, brahmin, kṣatriya, vaiśya, or śūdra; or a woman, man, boy, or girl—[should take up] this Amoghapāśahṛdaya, which is honored by all bodhisattvas.
Beholding the great cloth-painting (*mahāduṣyapaṭa*), which is the secret of the maṇḍala of great enlightenment observed by all the Tathāgatas and the secret of the maṇḍala of liberation, one shall,
by the mere sight of that cloth-painting, become completely liberated from all sins and obscurations.
For one who has committed the five deeds of immediate retribution and is destined for the Avīci hell,

or who rejects the true Dharma, or slanders the noble ones— by merely seeing [this], all sins, including the disparagement of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas, are utterly destroyed and one is liberated.
And he shall be embraced by the great vow;

it should be understood that he is equal to those who have approached the seat of awakening in person, turned the wheel of Dharma, and beheld the assembly circle within the palatial mansion arising on Mount Potalaka, [all occurring] through hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of grains of sand from ninety-nine Ganges rivers.
This vision of the noble Avalokiteśvara face-to-face is equal to the vision of this cloth painting; herein no doubt or hesitation should be conceived.
By means of a single moment of clarity of mind, he will be embraced by a great mass of merit;
he will be endowed with the planting of great roots of virtue.
The noble Avalokiteśvara will hold him in his memory and grant him his heart's desire;
moreover, he will be protected by all the Tathāgatas.
He will possess a completely pure mind and body;
he will have all his faculties purified, and he will be free from stains, having abandoned stinginess and envy. [He will be] endowed with all pleasant forms...
He shall be free from affliction and shall be long-lived;
he shall be free from all diseases.
Having passed away from this state of existence, he will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī.
He will remember his births;
he will be born from spontaneously appearing lotuses;
and he will become irreversible.
Merely by seeing the Tathāgata Amitābha,
whoever shall worship this cloth painting has thereby worshipped all the Tathāgatas in the ten directions.
This is the final birth from dwelling in a womb;
he shall no longer fall into the darkness of ignorance.
Thus, this ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the supramundane, which is equal to the unequally equal, is supreme.
Therefore,
I shall explain the mantra ritual, the supramundane accomplishment, by the mere recollection of which all the Tathāgatas remain present before one’s eyes.
The doors to all buddha-fields in the ten directions will be opened;
they will behold the direct vision of all bodhisattvas.
They will provide protection, defense, and concealment for the deities of all maṇḍalas in their very presence;
the ritual manuals of the heart-mantras of all maṇḍalas will become manifest before them, and they will become purified for proceeding upon the supramundane path.
Homage to him who, following the three sounds, is firmly established.
Homage to all those Tathāgatas and to the supreme assembly of the noble Great Bodhisattvas; homage to the noble Vajradhara and all the deities of the maṇḍala.
To the Kings of Knowledge:
Oṃ! To the one of unfailing vision, the great maṇḍala-lotus, who is honored by all bodhisattvas;
fill, fill, O you who look upon all!
Amogha, wearer of the great Brahma-robe;
Dhara, Dhara, O Great Compassionate One;
awaken, awaken, O Great Awakening!
O Awakening, O Awakening, awakener of the lotus!
You are the pacifier of the darkness of all evil, the great compassionate one who wards off all miserable rebirths;
you wear many diverse guises and possess the essence of all Tathāgatas.
Huru huru, O you whose womb is unfailing!
Turu turu, O you who hold the unfailing noose in your hand! Muru muru, O you whose arms grant liberation!
Kṣiṇi kṣiṇi, O you who are purified of all obscurations!
Bhara bhara, O you who are fulfilled by all the Tathāgatas!
Tara tara, deliver us!
Behold him, O lotus-handed one!

O you whose arms are adorned with jewels and gold; subdue, subdue those who are difficult to tame! O bestower of boons, O great Bodhisattva, O Great Compassionate One, saluted by the hosts of all gods and praised by the hosts of ṛṣis; illuminated by rays of light surpassing a hundred thousand moons and suns;
wearing the guise of Mahāpaśupati; O Supreme Pure Being!
O Avalokita, Lord of the World, Great Lord, Sovereign of the Maṇḍala of Supreme Compassion, Well-Awakened One, Great Lotus-Armed Lord, Sovereign of the Great Vidyādharas!

Steadfast, steadfast, O Greatly Steadfast One, Greatly Compassionate One, Bearer of the Maṇḍala of Great Liberation, Bearer of the Secret Mudrā-Samaya of all Tathāgatas, Bearer of Great Power and Heroic Vigor!
Wearing a crown of great jewels;
wearing a crown of Amitābha;
dhuru dhuru, O Samantāvalokeśvara, Maheśvara, Lord who holds the noose!
O you who have transcended the beyond, O Great Supreme Loving-kindness, O Avalokita, the deliverer of all sentient beings, the perfection of perfections, the fulfiller of hopes!
O bestower of the great boon, homage be to you, svāhā!
This is the maṇḍala of all liberations;
it is honored by all bodhisattvas;

it is the secret of all Tathāgatas, the supreme heart-secret of Noble Avalokiteśvara; it purifies all obscurations and misdeeds, purifies the supramundane path, and is the entrance into the family of all Tathāgatas.
Thus [it is said].

Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who follow throughout the three times! Oṃ, Hero, Hero, you who fulfill the six perfections through the manifold forms of the great maṇḍala, you who are honored by all bodhisattvas, you who possess the supreme, vast liberation, O Mahāpāśavilokita!

The Great Blazing Amoghapāśa, the Great Radiance Avalokiteśvara who holds the brilliance of the great jewel, who illuminates all directions; blaze, blaze! You who hold the noose of the great, profound liberation;

you who attract the powers and the factors of enlightenment; Oṃ, Brahma-form, Great Amoghapāśa, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ! O you who look upon all sentient beings, bestower of boons, homage be to you, svāhā! This is the heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa, the mandala of liberation, a supramundane miraculous manifestation.
Homage to the Three Jewels!
Homage to the Noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Greatly Compassionate One!
Oṃ, awaken, awaken, awaken, O Greatly Compassionate One!
Tara tara, ferry [us] across to the further shore of the great ocean; O mighty-armed one, look upon us! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
The minor heart-mantra.
Homage to all the Tathāgatas! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One!

Oṃ Amoghapāśa, fulfill the great perfection of generosity! Hūṃ! Dara dara! With various and manifold floods of offerings consisting of the great gifts of all the Tathāgatas for the enjoyment of all sentient beings, cause them to proceed!
Tara tara! Deliver! O Mahāpadmapāṇi! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

This is the Heart-Mantra of the Great Noose of the Perfection of Generosity (*dānapāramitāmahāpāśahṛdaya*). If one should give even a gift as small as a mustard seed, by the mere recollection of it and by reciting it seven times, there occurs a great, vast, and extensive miraculous display of sacrifice and giving, and one becomes perfected in the perfection of generosity.
Homage to all Tathāgatas! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One!
Oṃ amoghasīla saṃbhara saṃbhara! Bhara bhara! O Mahāśuddhasattva, whose arms are adorned with lotuses, dhara dhara! O Samantāvalokita, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

This dhāraṇī, when recited twenty-one times without speaking while observing the fast and being embraced by the noble eightfold path, and then the Amoghapāśahṛdaya being chanted— immediately upon its being chanted, one will become endowed with perfectly pure ethical discipline;
one becomes perfected in the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā).
They shall emit from their bodies a great fragrance, like the sweet scent of the *śīlasaugandhika* lotus,
which will spread throughout the worlds of the ten directions;
and whoever recites this dhāraṇī day after day [shall attain this].
And he shall always be endowed with perfectly pure morality.
Monks, this should be recited by one who has observed the fast with unbroken morality;
and as soon as it is recited, he becomes one of perfectly pure morality and shall be endowed with great morality.

Homage to all Tathāgatas! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! Oṃ, O you of great and unfailing vision! Grant, grant! O you of firm vigor, of great power, of strength upon strength, O limb of great awakening!
labodhyani (12) hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
When one recollects this dhāraṇī, through that mere recollection, perfectly pure mental attentions will arise, and the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) will be fulfilled.
Furthermore, one shall never be separated from the perfection of vigor until reaching the end at the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa).

Homage to all the Tathāgatas! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! Oṃ amoghakṣānti, you who endure for the sake of all Bodhisattvas, endure, endure! O you who possess great loving-kindness and compassion, who are affectionate toward sentient beings like a parent toward a child, O Great Compassionate One, you who endure all sentient beings! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

By means of this dhāraṇī, with a mind of great patience, great compassion, and universal pity for all sentient beings— for those who have passed away, those who currently abide, and those who have arisen among the inhabitants of hell, those born in the animal realm, and those who are wild beasts and birds— one should cause them to remember this supreme dhāraṇī. By this, the beings in hell are liberated, and many people who currently abide [in the world] become perfected in the perfection of patience (kṣāntipāramitā).
...until he is established in a Buddha-field. || ||
Homage to all the Tathāgatas! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Greatly Compassionate One!
Oṃ, the great unfailing meditative concentration and samādhi of the compassion of all the Tathāgatas, unshakable by any liberation; *curu curu* hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

By means of this dhāraṇī, with one-pointed attention, while taking the noble Avalokiteśvara as one’s object and recollecting him, through that mere recollection, one becomes fully perfected in the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*).
Furthermore, there will be the attainment of hundreds of thousands of other samādhis.
One will enter into all buddha-fields;
by mere recitation, one will become a master of samādhi everywhere.

Homage to all the Tathāgatas! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! Oṃ, you who possess the wisdom that radiates everywhere through the light of unfailing great insight; spread forth, spread forth, you whose wisdom is universal!
Behold, Blessed One, with the eye of the vision of insight (prajñā)! O you whose hand grants the boon of great insight, O holder of the lotus of great insight in your arm! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
By merely recollecting this Dhāraṇī, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) becomes complete; various forms of great wisdom, skillful means, and intelligence increase.
One will constantly and perpetually possess an intellect that follows the ten perfections (daśapāramitā).
Then, in all ten directions, there will arise for him the wisdom and intellect that recollects all the Tathāgatas— past, future, and present—
and he shall never again be separated from the six perfections,
nor from generosity, ethical discipline, and patience.
They will be devoid of morality, vigor, meditation, wisdom, and intelligence;
yet they shall not be deluded until they reach the culmination of enlightenment.
The Dhāraṇī of the Six Unfailing Perfections.
Homage to the Three Jewels!
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One!
It is thus: Oṃ, you who are the unerring, the circle of liberation, the great wonder, the stainless one!
Dhara dhara dhiri dhiri, bearing the great and wondrous lotus and the crown of Amitābha, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Having consecrated the mantra for drawing the mandala, along with mustard seeds, scented water, and a water-pot, one should sprinkle it all around.
As soon as it is sprinkled, the ground within a circumference of one yojana will become purified through the preparatory rites;
indeed, this surface of the earth will become as radiant, clear, and utterly stainless as a great crystal jewel.
The ground will become perfectly pure, utterly stainless, most delightful, and very charming;
and the regions of that ground (or those regions of women) will become excellent portions of land.
Whether they be women, men, boys, girls, śramaṇas, brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, or śūdras— all of them shall be established on the stage of non-retrogression;
all of them shall become irreversible and,
upon passing away, will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī.
They will remember their births from lifetime to lifetime;
they will have planted a great mass of merit and great roots of virtue,
until they fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
And those wild animals and birds belonging to the animal realm who enter and step upon that spot—
all of them shall become completely liberated.
They shall become those who have set out upon the path of the Sugata.
And all those who touch that clay held in the hand shall be free from disease, free from afflictions, free from fever, unobstructed, and free from evil.
Furthermore, no more bodily sensations of pain or disease will arise for them;
their bodies shall be perpetually endowed with bliss.
The Knowledge-mantra for Purifying the Grounds (14).
Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One!

Namely: Oṃ! O you who are unfailing! O tree, creeper, plant, branch, leaf, flower, fruit, and spreading bough! O you who cause growth! O river, pond, lotus-pool, lake, and beautiful mountain spring! Purify, purify!
Equally, equally, on all sides, in a perfect circle, purify! Mala mala! O stainless one, O pure one, O you who are well-purified and adorned with lotuses!
*jalamalāṃ viśuddha śodhaya śodhaya paramamahāśuddhasatva hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | namo tribhuvane hūṃ phaṭ svāhā |* With this [mantra], [one should offer] sandalwood and lotus.
Having recited [the mantra] over mustard seeds mixed with water, [one should sprinkle them upon] a tree trunk, a flowering tree,
or a fruit-bearing tree.

The various kinds of trees, grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, rivers, lakes, ponds, pools, lotus-pools, springs, and cascades— this beautiful [place] he sprinkles from above, and they all become drenched with nectar.
They shall all become divine flowers and fruits; even down to the divine grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, and forest trees,
they shall become so for those who merely touch them as soon as they are touched.
They shall all become free from the stains of stinginess and envy;
their bile, phlegm, and mucus shall be eliminated, and those with foul-smelling bodies shall become completely purified both internally and externally.
Furthermore, those whose internal bodies are afflicted by various diseases and ailments shall all be fully liberated, purified, and healed; they shall become utterly pure and stainless.
And those who bathe him with that water will have bathed with divine water and the waters of the factors of enlightenment;
they will have bathed from all stains, evils, and obscurations;
they will have bathed with the water of the eightfold path.
And those who shall chew that tooth-stick will have their mindfulness, intelligence, and wisdom greatly increased;
they will become free from all sorrow.
He is completely freed from all fetters,
and a lotus fragrance constantly wafts from his mouth.
He will have speech that is affectionate and sweet; he will be one whose words are gentle;
he will be one who speaks with kindness.
He will be beloved and pleasing to all people;
he will become a lord of the kinnaras;
and [he will master] all treatises, rituals, and mantras.
(15) 4. From merely hearing it, one comprehends;
it remains at the tip of the mouth.
And those who smell that flower or bind it as a garland shall become bound with the garland of the flowers of the factors of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga).
He shall be consecrated by the empowerment of the Tathāgatas;
his sense of smell shall be purified;
and he shall be endowed with the touch of divine fragrances.
His tongue will be pure like a lotus petal;
his teeth will have a color like those of the divine ones. Whomever he addresses, that person—whether woman or man—will always [be devoted].
Having passed away, he will come under the control of six young men and young women;
after a transition of births, he will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī.
He will be born from spontaneously appearing lotuses and will possess the recollection of his births in every lifetime.
[This applies to] fruits, flowers, water-born plants, grasses, shrubs, and medicinal herbs.
The mantra for purification.
Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One!
It is as follows: Oṃ amogha amale tṛmale vimale nirmale divyapariśuddhe sarvamalopakarṣite!
O bestower of boons to the great bodhisattvas, most excellently pure;

O you whose body is purified by great jewel-treasures, O jewel among jewels, purifier; O you who are pure as the great wish-fulfilling gem that is never in vain; O you whose heart is pure, whose body is stainless, and who are perfectly pure through the great jewel.
Huru huru, O you with excellent hands and mighty arms! Turu turu, O you who are compassionate toward great beings!
Purify me from all sins, O you of perfectly pure essence! Svāhā!
By means of this vidyā, the vidyādhara should purify his own body.

One should fill a new earthen jar with water mixed with sandalwood, saffron, *kāstūrikā*, camphor, mustard seeds, and the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). This should be consecrated by reciting this *vidyā* one thousand and eight times, and [the image] should be bathed with a white cloth.
Seven times...
One should drink seven *palas* [of it]. Immediately upon bathing, one should consecrate oneself with the King of Wrath (*krodharāja*).
Merely by bathing immediately and being consecrated, one’s own self will become perfectly pure and stainless both internally and externally;
one will be free from the obscurations and defilements of sin,
and free from the afflictions and diseases of the mental defilements.
They shall be free from old age and other such afflictions;
they shall be completely liberated from all obstacles, Vināyakas, Māras, and the like; and they shall be shunned by all yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, and piśācas.

Furthermore, one will not be able to approach the presence of a Vidyādhara for the purpose of creating obstacles; he accomplishes the vidyā easily, sleeps easily, wakes easily, and dwells happily throughout his life.
Having abandoned all impurities, he beholds all the Tathāgatas and beholds the Bodhisattvas.
Upon the completion of their life, they will behold the face of the noble Avalokiteśvara and, together with that very being, will be reborn in the world-realm of Sukhāvatī.
They will be born spontaneously from lotuses in the presence of the Tathāgata Amitābha, adorned with every ornament.
His body will be adorned with the primary and secondary marks, he will be born into noble lineages and possess the memory of his past lives,
and he will travel from buddha-field to buddha-field until he reaches the culmination of awakening.
And this *Vimokṣamaṇḍala* and the ritual manual (*kalpa*) of the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, entirely completed, shall remain present before their mouths;
as well as various other diverse and wonderful scriptures spoken by the Tathāgata, which shall likewise remain present before their mouths.
Within an interval of a hundred thousand eons, he will remember his births.
Oṃ, O Amogha-padmavimalā, who radiates forth from all directions, svāhā!
The mantra for the division of the instructions on the mandala lines.
Oṃ, to the one with unfailing and manifold forms, filled with various fragrances and tastes, and possessing most excellent arms—svāhā!
This is the mantra for painting, consisting of the arrangement of colors, mantras, forms, divisions, signs, and weapons.
Oṃ, you who are bound by the noose of the unerring, all-encompassing mandala! Hūṃ!
Bind the mandala with mustard seeds over which the mantra has been recited seven times.
Oṃ, O you who are the unfailing great boundary-binding in all ten directions! Dhuru dhuru hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
The binding of the boundary is performed with mustard seeds and water over which the mantra has been recited seven times.
Oṃ amogharakṣaṇapāśahaste bhuru bhuru svāhā!
Self-protection [is achieved] with mustard seeds and scented water over which this has been recited seven times.
Oṃ amoghacūḍāmaṇi huru huru, bound by the nāga-noose, hūṃ svāhā!
The mantra for binding the topknot (*śikhābandha*) is: *oṃ amogharakṣā samantena mahāpāśe bhuru bhuru svāhā*. It should be recited twenty-one times.
The protective mantras for the disciples and companions, as well as protection by means of mustard-seed ashes, should be performed with [the following] recited twenty-one times:
*oṃ amoghajalavimale suru suru svāhā*.
(17) The bathing mantra: with the *gandhodaka* over which the mantra has been recited twenty-one times.
Oṃ amogha amṛtabindu cara cara svāhā.
The mantra for sipping water.
Oṃ amoghavidyāvastre curu curu svāhā.
The mantra for the garment.
Oṃ amoghabhujaga-kavaca-varade ciri ciri svāhā.
The armor-mantra [is applied] with mustard seeds and saffron water.
Oṃ, O you whose arms are unfailing like those of Brahmā, spread forth to the limits! Svāhā!
The mantra for the sacred thread (yajñopavīta).
Oṃ amoghacūḍāmaṇipadme, empower me with the empowerments of all the Tathāgatas! Maṇi maṇi svāhā! This is the empowerment mantra. Oṃ amoghapadmavasu...
ndhare dhare dhara dharaṇimaṇḍe hūṃ ||
The mantra for the seat:
Oṃ amoghasamantaparyaṅke bhuvanabhuve svāhā.
88a 1. The Paryaṅka Mantra: Oṃ amoghasurabhipadme para para hūṃ.
The Flower Mantra: Oṃ amoghavividhagandhaprasaraiḥ puru pūrṇṇabhuje svāhā.
The mantra for incense:
Oṃ amoghavividhalepanapravare piri piri svāhā.
The mantra for the unguent:
Oṃ amoghagaganasphuraṇamaye dhūra dhūra hūṃ.
The incense mantra:
Oṃ amogha-śukla-rasa-rasāgra-dhara vidhara hūṃ.
The mantra for the bali offering.
One who is possessed of all the branches of knowledge.
Oṃ, O you who gaze upon the most excellent and unfailing [beings]!
Kiri kiri hūṃ!
The mantra for the offering of food:
Oṃ vividhāmoghamaghama(pha)la para para hūṃ.
The mantra of the fruit.
Oṃ, to the supreme, wondrous, and unfailing fragrance, hūṃ!
The mantra for the water offering (argha).
Oṃ, O you who possess the most excellent and supreme ornaments of various unfailing jewels! Blaze, blaze! Hūṃ!
The mantra of the five-colored thread for the decorative cloth-banner arrows.
Oṃ, O you who possess various unfailing vessels, victory! Victory! Svāhā!
The vessel-mantra is common to all three.
Oṃ, to the ground of the supreme and unfailing palace, thara thara svāhā!
The mantra of entry.
Oṃ amoghanamaskaraṇa-sarvata-tathāgata-añjali hūṃ.
The mantra for the salutation with palms joined in reverence.
Oṃ amoghacakre duru duru praduru svāhā. This is the mantra for circumambulation. Oṃ amoghasamanta yāntu bhavane bhava bhava svāhā.
The invocation mantra.
Oṃ, O unfailing wish-fulfilling gem, bring forth, dhuru dhuru, svāhā!
The mantra of supplication.
Oṃ, in the maṇḍala of the liberation through the unfailing invocation, mili mili svāhā!
The mantra for the invitation.
Oṃ, to the thousand blazing flames of the great unfailing light, blaze, blaze, O all-pervading one, svāhā!
The mantra of the lamp.
Oṃ, O you who hold the unfailing noose in your hand, go forth! Enter the abode; you are now released! Move on, move on! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
The mantra for dismissal.
Oṃ, O firm one of the great universal samaya that binds with the unfailing noose, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
This is the samaya-mantra.
Oṃ, O you of unfailing universal presence, most excellent one, move, move, spread forth! O Lord of the great elements, dhiri dhiri, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

With this mantra, one should offer a bali of sweetmeat balls (laḍḍuka), modakas, flour-meal, roots, tubers, and white offerings to Mahāgaṇapati. By causing flowers and incense to be offered, it is no longer possible for obstacles to arise.
Now, I shall describe the mudrās and the supramundane maṇḍala.
By merely grasping this, all evils are destroyed;

it shatters the afflictions, the obscurations of karma, and every defilement. This is the reality of the *samayamudrā* of the family of the *vimokṣamaṇḍala*. Place the lotus [mudrā] in the hand, with the thumbs joined together.
With both hands joined in the form of the middle hook,
this mudrā is the Samaya of Liberation, empowered as the Amoghapāśa;
it is the extraordinary supramundane [attainment] that brings about the path to the fruit.
Oṃ, to the one with lotus arms, the one with lotus hands, the one pure as a lotus, svāhā!
The wise one, supreme among the foremost of those who hold the commitments, should always form the vajra-lotus; with the middle fingers slightly contracted,
it is always held in the shape of a lotus in the hand.
For whomsoever this seal of vision exists in the world, they shall attain incomparable sovereignty.
Through the seal of liberation, there is no doubt that they shall attain incomparable Buddhahood.
This seal, the wondrous mandala of liberation, is honored by all bodhisattvas.
Oṃ padme supadme, O you who hold in your hand the lotus of the maṇḍala of liberation, svāhā!

Having established the *padmabandha*, one should contract the *vajrapadma* with the middle fingers; this is the secret seal (*mudrā*) of the liberation of all Tathāgatas, which reveals the reality of liberation. Merely by seeing this seal, all misdeeds are destroyed. (19) Oṃ amoghe vajrapadmabhuje mili mili svāhā.
The two palms joined at the wrists in the form of a vajra constitute the Cintāmaṇi mudrā;
it performs unfailing deeds, raining down the supreme worship of Amogha.
Fulfilling the six perfections unfailingly, the unfailing vision of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
the unfailing secret mandala of liberation that purifies the five deeds of immediate retribution:
Oṃ amoghamaṇi maṇi mahāmaṇi padmamaṇi svāhā!

One should form the *vajrapadma* (or *vajrapadmā*) añjali; this mudrā, in which the middle fingers are shaped like hooks and the [thumb and index fingers] are skillfully separated like a lotus, is most beautiful, visible to those capable of seeing it, and yields great and wondrous fruit.
And there is the vision of the Buddhas of the three times, which is supramundane and distinguished.
Oṃ amoghavajre mahāpadme añjali sujali mahājali svāhā.

The two lotuses of the vajra-heart and the complete vajra-binding, pressing the threatening fingers into the shape of a hook—this mudrā possesses great splendor and great strength and prowess; it is the locus that effects all accomplishments and bestows all accomplishments. 3.
The unsurpassed, supreme great accomplishment for the sake of Buddhahood;
the unsurpassed accomplishment that removes all sins:
Oṃ amoghasiddhe sarvatathāgatasiddhe avalokaya siddhe mahāvipulasiddhe kuru kuru svāhā!
Having placed the hands in the lotus-añjali gesture, one should likewise stand with the body perfectly upright;
then, opening the little fingers and thumbs, one should slightly bend only the middle fingers.

The great being Māpadmeśvara, as well as the teacher Lokeśvara, and the maṇḍala of liberation, which is always honored by all bodhisattvas—thus, this is the mudrā of the heart of Amoghapāśa. By the sight of this mudrā, one becomes equal to the sight of Lokeśvara; this supreme mudrā of sight is equal to the maṇḍala of liberation.
One attains the state of non-retrogression.

By the mere sight and engagement with the seal (mudrā), for one who knows the samaya in all respects, there shall be the immediate attainment of the fruit through the mere sight and grasping of it; immediately, one attains the unsurpassed awakening of a Buddha.
Homage to the Three Jewels!
Homage to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva, the Mahāsattva, the Great Compassionate One!
Oṃ! O you who have beheld the great pure being! Move, move! You who wear earrings that illuminate all directions!
Wearing a crown of Amitābha, adorned with a crown of matted locks, a new vajra, and the moon—*cara cara sambhara bhuvaneśvarapadmabhuje svāhā*.
These seven are the great mudrās that reveal the supramundane fruit;
they are the revealers of the path to the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*) and the turners of the wheel of Dharma.
The meditation on the Lord of the World, the eternal teacher Lokeśvara, consists of the seven mudrās; Mahāmudrā is surrounded by a retinue of seventy million.
These seven are the Mahāmudrās wherein they operate.
The seven million supreme mudrās are set forth; they are grasped. All of them become honored and venerated.
They become honored;
they are captivated by the grasping of their names.
These seven great mudrās accomplish mantras everywhere.
Applicable everywhere in all rites, this all-accomplishing mudrā is the unsurpassed path that transcends the world.

The practitioner who, having bathed thoroughly and remained pure, performs this mudrā of manifestation and vision, shall not go to an evil rebirth or hell. By the mere performance of this mudrā, they immediately behold their former obscurations in the presence of seven hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of perfectly enlightened Buddhas.
He will have planted roots of merit;
he will have accumulated a great mass of merit;
and he will have fulfilled the six perfections.
He will be established in the ten stages;
he attains the state of non-retrogression.
Even one who has committed the five acts of immediate retribution, who has rejected the true Dharma, or who has slandered the noble ones—[shall attain this].
Even those whose ultimate destination is the Avīci hell— if they merely grasp the seal or behold it— even now, all these evil deeds will perish;
they shall be embraced by all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
He shall be protected by all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, and piśācas.
Īśvara, Maheśvara, the four Great Kings, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Kumāra will always follow him and constantly provide protection, defense, and guardianship.
He will be pleasing to behold for all sentient beings.
And through the equality of the non-substantiality of all things, he will possess a body that is a treasury of the elements;
he will possess a body as solid as a diamond.
Neither poison, nor fire, nor weapons, nor water, nor a destructive wind, nor the fear of rats shall overcome him.
Neither lion, nor fierce beast, nor venomous serpent, nor thief, nor robber;
neither loss of home, nor furthermore the seizure of yakṣas, rākṣasas, or grahas, nor any disease shall overcome him.
No fear of poison, *kākhorda*, or magical spells shall assail his body, nor shall he ever see evil dreams.
One will constantly behold the vision of the Tathāgata;
one will behold the vision of the Bodhisattva;
and there will always be the vision of the noble Avalokiteśvara.
And he will constantly be a granter of boons;
and all the deities will always and perpetually desire to behold him.
And his virtue and merit will constantly blaze forth;
moreover, his body will become resplendent with glory.
And he will be greatly honored everywhere;
he will be greatly honored by kings, ministers, brahmins, and householders, along with their harems and retinues.

Even as far as the thirty-two celestial abodes, they will desire to worship him; he will become highly worthy of veneration by Śakra, the lord of the gods of the Thirty-three, and by the deities Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Kumāra, and the hosts of ṛṣis.
Furthermore, all sentient beings will constantly have a longing to behold him.
And they shall constantly desire to behold him with affection.
The Vidyādhara must be well-bathed, pure, and dressed in clean garments; his body should be anointed with various perfumes and scented with various incenses.

One should smear both arms with white sandalwood and saffron, scented with camphor and musk. Sitting cross-legged on a pure spot of ground, or before a cloth or silk banner, or before an image of the Buddha, or before the noble Avalokiteśvara, one should perform this mudrā; one should perform the mudrā in front of a caitya containing relics.
Through the ritual procedure for worshipping the Buddha, by means of the offering of water for the feet and the guest-water,
one should possess a mind of loving-kindness and compassion;
one should be devoted to benevolence toward all sentient beings, with a heart encompassed by great compassion.
One should regard all sentient beings as if they were an only son.
One should maintain mental attention upon the noble Avalokiteśvara;
one should cultivate mindfulness through mental attention upon the Buddha.
This should be set in motion as the seven great mudrās;
thus, seven crores of mudrās will have been set in motion.
Now I shall explain "proximity" (*sāṃnidhya*); proximity is the vision of supramundane reality. (22)
And the manifestation of the Amoghapāśa, the direct vision of his own natural body, [is seen] either by the king, or in the midst of the inner apartments,
or among great people, or in a great assembly, or in the midst of the Saṅgha, or indeed within a community of monks.

In the assembly of the four castes—among the community of śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, women, men, boys, girls, vaiśyas, and śūdras—he perceives them directly before his eyes. Therein, he immediately witnesses the miraculous manifestation of the Amoghapāśa:

those who have passed away and been reborn in the supramundane realms, as well as those of the past, future, and present, [he sees] according to their true nature—their births, their actions, and the fruits of those actions.

Through the merit or demerit of death and rebirth, one may obtain sovereignty or poverty, the status of a king, divine enjoyments, or the thirty-two celestial abodes; or else the state of Śakra, or eternally the state of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, or Maheśvara;
or birth among the Nagas, Pretas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, or Guhyakas.
The appearance of the terrible hell Avīci at its very limit,

or birth in a family of Brahmins or Kṣatriyas, as well as birth in various other assemblies of families— all this is seen as if directly before one's eyes through the power of the Lord of the World; everything that is achievable by worldly karma is thus manifested.
Victory and defeat, security and famine, as well as scarcity, pestilence, and calamity;
whether it be the enemy's army or one's own army, adversaries and rivals, or even the battle itself.
Long life or short life, illness or health;

rain, excessive rain, drought, or untimely rain; sovereignty or its loss, prosperity or misfortune; arrival or departure, the acquisition of wealth and grain, increase or decrease, or whatever sight of famine may occur—whatever [it may be].

Whether actions currently being performed are essential or not, whether they are well-done or ill-done, wholesome or unwholesome, or whether they lead to decline or increase; whether there will be birth, a good birth, the gain of a son, the gain of a daughter, a virtuous son, or an unworthy son; or whether the one dwelling in the womb is meritorious or lacking merit—this vision is true.
Through the application of well-performed rites, there is no doubt.

Neither a lunar day nor a constellation, nor even a specific day or night, is prescribed. Only the recitation (*jāpa*) and the offering (*bali*) are required; likewise, one must be pure, having bathed well with great cleanliness, wearing clean garments, speaking the truth, possessing a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*), serving the teacher, and, O upholder, consuming pure food and drink while avoiding mixed or impure food.

One who desires excellence should avoid liquor, meat, onions, garlic, leeks, food prepared from impure mixtures, and the remnants of another's meal; by avoiding these, one should perform this rite, for direct perception is seen everywhere as the means to achieve the goal.
One who observes the vow should not treat others with contempt, nor should he show disrespect; one must never act [thus] even behind their back. This is the instruction for the supreme one.
Thus spoke the Lord, the Sovereign of the World:
"Having fashioned a mirror made of silver, perfectly circular on all sides..."
One should fashion an image of the noble Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa upon a mirror with a handle measuring one cubit in length and a lotus seat sixteen finger-breadths in width.

It should be made either of silver or of gold; the lotus seat should measure four finger-breadths, and he should be depicted with four arms, holding a trident, a noose, a lotus, and a jewel. Having thoroughly cleansed it so that it is well-polished and brilliantly radiant, it should be purified.
Then the vidyādhara should place the relics of the body of Avalokiteśvara into the mirror; the body [of the image] should be filled with camphor and musk.
Around the entire mirror, a garland inlaid with silver, gold flowers, and various jewels should be fastened.

Then, day by day at the three junctions of the day, the vidyādhara should recite the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya one hundred and eight times over that mirror and consecrate it with the King of Wrath (Krodharāja), until [the number reaches] eight thousand.
Then a full mirror blazes forth;
it becomes a single flame of various colors,
and from that image of Lokeśvara, divine water flows.
Various rays of light stream forth;
thereupon, the body of the vidyādhara blazes and rejoices.

One who attains the accomplishment of the ritual manual (*kalpa*) of the Heart of the Amoghapāśa, named "The Immaculate Joy of Unfailing Bliss," shall possess a body that is perfectly stainless and utterly pure.
Then the vidyādhara must demonstrate the accomplishment of the miraculous transformations of Amoghapāśa before the eyes of all the world.
Then,
having prepared a square mandala smeared with clay and cow dung,
the vidyādhara should construct a cloth canopy four cubits in width and two cubits in height, which is very smooth and well-finished.
And it should be constructed by dividing it with the cord of the sūtra into various color divisions,
distinguished by four gates. (24)

Divide the center into a mandala lotus with one hundred and eight petals, variegated and skilled in colors, with a circle of filaments and a pericarp. The circumference of the lotus is square, adorned with various jewels and decorated with a railing (*vedikā*). And in the four corners of the railing, one should draw the four Great Kings.
One should draw deities who are armored, bound in mail, fierce in form, and terrifying,

situated in the locations of the middle and intermediate altars. One should draw the deities Īśvara, Maheśvara, Yama, Varuṇa, Kuvera, Kumāra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Indra, Vajrapāṇi, Ekajaṭā, Tārā, Śvetā, Bhṛkuṭī, and Vajradūtī.
All [the attendants] should be adorned with every kind of ornament and made to hold various multicolored flowers in their hands.
Outside the enclosure, a garland of tridents should be made, as well as a garland of vajras and a garland of lotuses all around.
Within the intervals between the garlands and in the interior corners of the four sides,
the eight goddesses are to be fashioned:
Bhīmā, Anopamya, Vāsantī, Śrī, Sarasvatī, and Pṛthivīdevatā.
Saṃkhinī and Puṣpadantī, adorned with all ornaments,
should be depicted holding various flowers and jeweled vessels.
Inside and outside the perimeter of the garland, one should smear the mandala with various fragrances and worship it in many ways with white sandalwood and saffron.
One should worship with camphor and musk, and adorn [the site] on all sides with circular mandalas, banners of five-colored silk, and archways made of reeds.
Four silver vessels filled to the brim with *pūrṇa* (fullness) should be placed;
and in four silver vessels, an offering of the three white substances (*triśuklabali*) should be filled.
Four silver vessels for the water of honor and the water for the feet should be set out. Eight vessels should be filled with offerings of various flavors.
Various kinds of fruits should be arranged;
various types of food and offerings should be set out;
and various perfumes, ointments, silver vessels, and roots should be placed there.
Eight silver bowls should be filled.
While burning various incenses— sandalwood, agallochum, turuṣka, camphor, musk, saffron, resin, and kunduruka— one should scatter silver, copper, and gold flowers upon the inner maṇḍala,
and [scatter them] upon the outer maṇḍalas.

Having scattered flowers as they were obtained over the outer mandala (25), one should arrange garlands all around; then, having made that mirror well-polished, it should be placed facing east upon the pericarp of the lotus filaments in the central mandala. The Vidyādhara must be pure, well-bathed, and wearing clean garments, and he must perform all the ritual activities pertaining to the mandala.

Having placed a mirror in front of oneself and sat down cross-legged, one should recite the Noble Amoghapāśahṛdaya. When the recitation is complete—having performed it one hundred and eight times—one should be consecrated by the King of Wrath (Krodharāja).

As soon as one is consecrated, the Noble Avalokiteśvara appears in his true form within the middle of that mirror, visible to the eyes of all the world in the midst of the great assembly; and from within the mirror, he gives his approval to the practitioner of mantra (vidyādhara).

"Excellent, excellent, O great vidyādhara! This which has been shown to me is truly unfailing; by means of the reality of entering the mirror, everything that is good is seen—the unsurpassed fruit of both mundane and supramundane actions."
"O Vidyādhara, you have attained complete purity and the incomparable supramundane path; thus, a great fruit has been achieved by you.
You have mastered the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*, including the mundane and supramundane methods of accomplishment, the ritual manuals (*kalpa*), mandalas, and mudrās.
Choose a boon, O Vidyādhara; I shall grant it all."
It is both mundane and supramundane.
Then, whatever excellent object the vidyādhara might say he would give, he would grant it all immediately.

And those who had assembled in that circle of the assembly— women, men, boys, girls, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, vaiśyas, kings, ministers, bhaṭṭas, domestic priests, and those gathered in the inner apartments— [all were present].
Whether they be meritorious or demeritorious, pure in intention or possessed of wrong views;

and whatever other beings there may be in the various hells, fallen into the darkness of delusion, headed for the Avīci hell, those who have committed the five deeds of immediate retribution, those who revile the noble ones, and those who reject the true Dharma— they too all behold that very form of the noble Avalokiteśvara.
He converses with all of them and comforts them;
he reveals to all of them the entire ripening of their own karma, whether it be auspicious or inauspicious.
Excepting that of a thief of knowledge, a caṇḍāla,
one who destroys a deposit of knowledge, a defiler of knowledge, or one who lacks faith and does not desire to hear— there is no vision of it for such a person.
Other various [obstacles] of one's own...

He sees that they have emerged from the fruits of the suffering of karma. Then those beings, in that great circle of the assembly, see all that which they had intended in their minds— whether worldly or supramundane— as having emerged as their respective fruits, seeing the fruit of both merit and demerit.
They see all the buddha-fields of the Tathāgatas;
they see the great bodies of the Tathāgatas together with their celestial palaces and mansions.
He beholds the celestial palace on Mount Potalaka, together with the Lord’s miraculous manifestations;
he sees the noble Avalokiteśvara with his assembly in that palace, surrounded by gods and nāgas.
Furthermore, he perceives other things as they actually exist, whether auspicious or inauspicious, such as times of plenty or famine.
Disease and death; short or long life; fear of one's own army or the enemy's army, or of war and battle; victory or defeat; that which is lost or destroyed;
pestilence, excessive rain, untimely rain, or drought.
Whether it be wind, cold, or heat, all that is seen as the arrival of wealth;
whether it be loss or gain,
or the increase of crops, flowers, and fruits— all that is seen.

Whether it be the fear of thieves, robbers, poison, or weapons; the fear of kings; or the fear of yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, ḍākinīs, and apasmāras—all that is seen. Or whether it be a great treasure—all that is seen.
And death and rebirth are seen;
the attainment of a son, or the attainment of a village, city, district, or country, or the attainment of a woman— all that is seen.
No doubt, no misapprehension, and no hesitation should be raised here;
this rite must be accomplished with great effort, supreme faith, and reverence.
Amoghapāśa, 91a 1. The procedure for the supramundane sādhana in the Vimokṣamaṇḍala is completed. (27)
